parsed_response.reasoning: The backend explicitly and intentionally defaults blank category_id: `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb. So a new row saved with categoryId null (because edit() was never called on an auto-editing isNew row, or the user left the chooser unset) does not 'silently land in the wrong category with no error' — it lands in uncategorized by design, matching the old SiteSetting behavior being migrated. The category-chooser template binds `value=categoryId`, so selecting a category sets it directly; the save path correctly forwards it. The 'duplicated host value in two places' claim mischaracterizes the standard buffered-content pattern (buffered.host is exactly what getProperties('host') reads). No verifiable defect in the described mechanism.

judged_text: save() sends only `host` and `category_id` derived from `this.categoryId`, which is set only in the edit() action — an unsaved-new-row path or a save without prior edit leaves categoryId null and the buffered host name is read via getProperties('host') while the input binds to `buffered.host`, duplicating the host value in two places. If save fires before edit() ever set categoryId (e.g. an enter-keypress race on a newly added row), the row is persisted with category_id null, which the backend silently rewrites to uncategorized — the admin sees their newly added host land in the wrong category with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `categoryId` is initialized to `null` and is only set in the `edit()` action (`this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))`). For a newly added host (`host.isNew` => `editing` true), `edit()` is never invoked, so unless the user changes the `{{category-chooser value=categoryId}}`, `save()` will send `props.category_id = null`. The backend (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) explicitly rewrites blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, so the record is persisted to uncategorized. Additionally, after save the UI sets `host.category` from `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, which will be `findById(null)` in this path, leaving the displayed category out of sync with what the server actually saved.
